why: Chloe never appears in this chapter's range, so the scene runs on the camera exception, which explicitly forbids interiority for anyone in it; this states Sam's felt preference directly rather than an observable fact.
suggestion: Open on an observable beat instead: "Sam salutes on the first morning and doesn't stop saluting a beat too long."

why: States Sam's inner feeling toward Ruiz; the camera exception governing this Chloe-less scene bans interiority for anyone in it, not just non-POV characters.
suggestion: Cut the clause and show the liking through behavior: "who shouts at him for four weeks while Sam keeps volunteering for the extra mile."

quote: it had not occurred to him that a test could be over
why: Direct rendering of a thought Sam has not had, the near-exact construction the style guide names as the banned example of other-character interiority ('It occurs to him that...').
suggestion: Cut the clause; the repeated, improved run already shows the compulsion without narrating it: "Then he does it again in week three, better."

quote: There is no version of a task in Sam's head
why: Explicitly narrates the contents of Sam's mind ('in Sam's head'), which the camera exception for this Chloe-absent scene forbids outright.
suggestion: Replace with an observable pattern: "He reruns the assessment three more times before anyone tells him to stop."

quote: because he has worked out that this must be a trick question and he doesn't want to embarrass the man
why: Reports Sam's private reasoning and motive rather than anything observable; a camera scene with no Chloe present may show only what happened and what was said.
suggestion: Cut the clause and let delivery carry it: "Sam says, slower now, like he's walking the captain through something."

quote: this is the moment he has been waiting four months for, because he has become increasingly certain that basic training is some kind of extended screening exercise and that there is a real one somewhere and that he is being kept out of it by not having said the right thing yet
suggestion: Cut to the observable action and let the next line do the work: "Sam takes that as an invitation."
why: A sustained block of Sam's private theory and hope, none of it visible to an outside observer; forbidden in this scene by the camera exception's ban on interiority for anyone.

rule_name: Banned Constructions, Assert Nothing, Show the Substance
quote: So he says the right thing.
why: The sentence's entire content is a verdict on correctness with no evidence supplied in it, the same pattern as the banned "the right way to do this."
suggestion: Cut the sentence and let the dialogue that follows stand on its own without the narrator pre-labeling it as correct.

quote: who has seen the name Halstead before, in a different context, some years ago
why: Builds an unresolved, ominous mystery about an unnamed character's private history entirely in the narrator's voice; the structure rules require mystery to live in a character's mouth, never in narration, and this is also interiority of a non-POV character in a scene with no Chloe present to license it.
suggestion: Cut the clause here and let the recognition surface later through something the woman actually says.

why: Routes the fact of Sam's ignorance through the filtering verb "knows" instead of rendering the gap directly.
suggestion: Render it as a scene fact instead: "Sam is three states away, doing push-ups."

quote: Sam is having a great month.
why: An unphysicalized label of Sam's internal state with nothing observable behind it, barred by the camera exception's rule that this Chloe-less scene may carry no one's interiority.
suggestion: Swap in an observable detail: "Sam is on his second helping of eggs."

rule_name: Bury Scale Inside a Fast List, Deliberately
quote: In month four they put him on a range with ten targets and tell him to shoot ten targets.
why: This opens roughly fifty lines of full dialogue scene built around the chapter's one truly extraordinary fact, a person who can put a round into another round in flight, while the ordinary material just before it (maxing and re-maxing the fitness test) was compressed into three summary sentences; the rule requires the reverse, extraordinary material buried in a fast list and ordinary material given the scene-time.
suggestion: Compress the marksmanship reveal into a fast, complete inventory (the range, the sheet, the captain's line, the number) and give the extended dialogue scene to something ordinary, like the day-to-day with Ruiz.
